targetTexts.1: Woe to you, O destroyer never destroyed, O traitor never betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed. When you have finished betraying, you will be betrayed.
targetTexts.2: O LORD, be gracious to us! We wait for You. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in time of trouble.
targetTexts.3: The peoples flee the thunder of Your voice; the nations scatter when You rise.
targetTexts.4: Your spoil, O nations, is gathered as by locusts; like a swarm of locusts men sweep over it.
targetTexts.5: The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
targetTexts.6: He will be the sure foundation for your times, a storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is Zion’s treasure.
targetTexts.7: Behold, their valiant ones cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
targetTexts.8: The highways are deserted; travel has ceased. The treaty has been broken, the witnesses are despised, and human life is disregarded.
targetTexts.9: The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and decayed. Sharon is like a desert; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
targetTexts.10: “Now I will arise,” says the LORD. “Now I will lift Myself up. Now I will be exalted.
targetTexts.11: You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble. Your breath is a fire that will consume you.
targetTexts.12: The peoples will be burned to ashes, like thorns cut down and set ablaze.
targetTexts.13: You who are far off, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My might.”
targetTexts.14: The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling grips the ungodly: “Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire? Who of us can dwell with everlasting flames?”
targetTexts.15: He who walks righteously and speaks with sincerity, who refuses gain from extortion, whose hand never takes a bribe, who stops his ears against murderous plots and shuts his eyes tightly against evil—
targetTexts.16: he will dwell on the heights; the mountain fortress will be his refuge; his food will be provided and his water assured.
targetTexts.17: Your eyes will see the King in His beauty and behold a land that stretches afar.
targetTexts.18: Your mind will ponder the former terror: “Where is he who tallies? Where is he who weighs? Where is he who counts the towers?”
targetTexts.19: You will no longer see the insolent, a people whose speech is unintelligible, who stammer in a language you cannot understand.
targetTexts.20: Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful pasture, a tent that does not wander; its tent pegs will not be pulled up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
targetTexts.21: But there the Majestic One, our LORD, will be for us a place of rivers and wide canals, where no galley with oars will row, and no majestic vessel will pass.
targetTexts.22: For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King. It is He who will save us.
targetTexts.23: Your ropes are slack; they cannot secure the mast or spread the sail. Then an abundance of spoils will be divided, and even the lame will carry off plunder.
targetTexts.24: And no resident of Zion will say, “I am sick.” The people who dwell there will be forgiven of iniquity.
